items.text: The Mississippi Senate race is turning into a legal fight. Hyde-Smith's lawyers and the NRSC sent letters to all 82 counties asking them to keep affidavit ballots separate and preserved. Colom's campaign wrote back calling the demand unlawful and a threat to ballot secrecy. AP had Colom ahead by about 1,138 votes, with roughly 3,600 mail ballots and thousands of affidavit ballots still to count.
items.notes: Decision Desk HQ put Colom's lead at 1,818. RedState frames the letters as a legitimate Republican salvage effort. Democracy Docket calls them a bid to throw out votes. State GOP chair Mike Hurst said the party would use every legal option if evidence emerges. Affidavit ballots can be cured until Nov 10, and counties must certify by Nov 13. The Colom campaign told CNN up to 15,000 affidavit ballots remain.

items.text: Alaska's Senate race is unchanged: Peltola leads Sullivan by 637 votes (48.2% to 47.9%) with about 70% reported. Neither has a majority, so a ranked-choice tabulation set for Nov 18 will probably decide it. An Alaska Beacon analysis found that ranked-choice transfers could help Sullivan.
items.outlet: Decision Desk HQ; Straight Arrow News
items.notes: Totals are from the DDHQ page updated Nov 5 at 16:55 EST. Second Republican Gerald Heikes has 2.3%, and his second choices would mostly go to Sullivan. I did not read the Alaska Beacon analysis in full; the title is https://alaskabeacon.com/2026/11/04/ranked-choice-voting-may-help-republican-us-sen-dan-sullivan-analysis-finds/. Sullivan's campaign has also published a memo saying he wins once ranked-choice votes are counted.

items.text: At least seven incoming Democratic senators have said or suggested they will not back Chuck Schumer for majority leader. Sen. Van Hollen and the group Indivisible want a contested leadership race. Schumer says he will be re-elected and promises investigations of the administration and a push to end the Iran war. The leadership vote is expected in December.
items.notes: The holdouts named are Stratton (IL), Hamilton (KS), Jackson (ME), El-Sayed (MI), Flanagan (MN), Pappas (NH) and Talarico (TX), though Talarico only said he wants to hear Schumer's vision first. Sen. Booker defended Schumer. Roll Call reports Thune will run for minority leader. I read only the headline of the Washington Times piece.

items.text: Trump signed a proclamation under the Antiquities Act making the Oval Office, the Outer Oval Office and the Cabinet Room a national monument. Interior must now document, review and consider alternatives before any major alteration or demolition, which is meant to discourage future presidents from changing the rooms.
items.outlet: White House fact sheet; Spectrum News
items.notes: Per the fact sheet, the order is a review requirement rather than an outright ban. Critics such as Jimmy Kimmel mocked Trump's gold makeover of the room. Whether a successor could simply revoke the proclamation is untested.

items.text: After meeting his security team on Nov 5, Trump said the US might have to destroy the rest of Iran and that a decision on resuming the war would come soon. Per two officials who spoke to Axios, he is weighing strikes, continued pressure or a deal. On Nov 6 he phoned Qatar's emir about Qatar's mediation, and the emir urged continued dialogue. Al Jazeera reports that Iran sent a nuclear proposal through Qatar, which Washington is reviewing.
items.reporter: Gulf News live team; Heba Habib et al. (Al Jazeera)
items.notes: Bloomberg also reports the Qatar call (paywalled, not read). The nuclear proposal comes only from Al Jazeera's summary, with no details. Iran says Hormuz stays closed until its seven conditions are met, and its army warns any new attack would bring strikes on US assets worldwide. Trump acknowledged 18 US service members have died. Iran's FM Araghchi called nine regional counterparts, and security chief Rezaei met Putin in Moscow. Brent rebounded to about $98 on Nov 6.

items.text: Iran's IRGC said two more tankers hit mines on Nov 6, one in the Strait of Hormuz and one east of it, after similar claims on Nov 5. The UK maritime agency separately reported a tanker hit by two projectiles about 50 nm north of Qatar on Nov 5. No maritime authority has confirmed the mine strikes. CENTCOM had earlier said the waterway was cleared of mines.
items.notes: The IRGC says the ships had switched off their navigation systems and were backed by the US military. UKMTO/JMIC counts four attacks in 96 hours off Musandam (1-3 Nov). Fars says the IRGC seized two US-built LUCAS drones. A Houthi missile was also intercepted near Medina and Najran, per the Saudi coalition.

items.text: A US official told CBS that the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group will call at Singapore and won't reach the Middle East for at least two weeks. Officials say the two carrier groups already there are enough.
items.notes: This suggests no immediate build-up despite Trump's threats. It comes from one anonymous official.

items.text: Some Republicans are publicly distancing themselves from the Iran war after the midterm loss. Sen. Cruz said it dragged on too long and objected to a proposed $300bn reconstruction fund, and Sen. Tillis said Hegseth faces a reckoning. Democrats are focusing on Congress's power of the purse: Rep. Khanna proposed a funding bill that would bar money for combat in Iran.
items.notes: Fox frames this as Trump weighing whether to resume the war, and Al Jazeera as allies abandoning him. Analyst Paul Musgrave expects funding fights rather than War Powers votes. I did not fully read the Fox live page.

items.text: US stocks had their worst day in months on Nov 5. The Dow fell about 1,833 points (3.4%), the S&P 500 fell 4.4% (its worst day since April 2025) and the Nasdaq fell 5.5%, putting it in correction. About $2.3–2.5tn in market value was wiped out. Chipmakers led the fall on fears that the Democratic sweep will slow AI data-centre spending: Micron and AMD fell about 17% and Nvidia 9%.
items.outlet: Stock Titan (citing CNBC, Reuters); Yahoo Finance
items.notes: This erased the Nov 4 rally. The VIX hit 28, its highest since March 31. Futures put the odds of a December Fed hike at about 70%, down from 83%. Early Nov 6, Nasdaq futures were up about 1% and Dow futures down about 1%. Brent was about $96–98.

items.text: Investors are focused on Democratic governors-elect who promised to curb data centres. In Texas, Gina Hinojosa (who takes office Jan 19) wants a moratorium on approvals until lawmakers pass protections. Ohio's Amy Acton proposed a conditional moratorium, and Georgia's Keisha Lance Bottoms promised a temporary statewide pause. Gov. Abbott has already paused grid hookups and environmental permits pending an audit due Dec 10.
items.notes: Both pieces link this backlash to the Nov 5 sell-off. Tech Times notes that the legal scope of any governor's moratorium is unclear. Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez have proposed a federal ban on data-centre construction (TechCrunch, not read).

items.text: Judge Trevor McFadden set jury selection for Sept 7, 2027 in the trial of Cole Tomas Allen. Allen is charged with attempting to assassinate Trump at the April 25 White House Correspondents' Dinner. Prosecutors expect a trial of up to four weeks. He has pleaded not guilty and faces up to life in prison.
items.notes: This is a late catch: the date was set at the Oct 29 status conference (watch W-261026-06), and the AP story ran Oct 30. The AP text says only 'next year', but OAN's headline confirms September 2027.

items.text: US District Judge Mae D'Agostino refused to block New York's 'Local Cops, Local Crimes Act', which bars local police from civil immigration enforcement and from ICE partnership agreements. Fifteen sheriffs had sued Gov. Hochul and AG James. The judge found they had not shown they had the capacity to bring the constitutional claims.
items.notes: AG James announced the ruling on Nov 4, but its exact date is not stated. It denies only a preliminary injunction, so the case continues. Twelve New York agencies had been told to end their ICE agreements.

items.text: Macleods Pharma is recalling about 3,700 bottles of a generic three-in-one blood-pressure pill (olmesartan, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide) because tests suggest the tablets may not dissolve properly. The FDA classed the recall as Class II.
items.outlet: The Digger News; Florida Poison Control
items.notes: The affected lots are 12251163A and 12251163B. Macleods is an Indian manufacturer. The articles don't give the date of the FDA classification. I did not read the second source in full.

items.text: An Oct 28 proclamation finds that imports of robotics and industrial machinery threaten national security under Section 232, but imposes no tariffs for now. Commerce and USTR will negotiate with trading partners and report by April 26, 2027. It follows the same pattern as the Oct 22 wind-turbine proclamation.
items.outlet: Trade Compliance Resource Hub (Reed Smith) tracker
items.notes: This is a late catch not covered earlier. No new tariff action was found for Nov 5-6. Nov 10 is the date tied to the delayed tariffs on maritime cargo-handling equipment and to China's suspended rare-earth export controls. I did not read the second source in full.

items.text: Anthropic's IPO roadshow could start as early as the week of Nov 9, according to Bloomberg as relayed by other outlets. A first trading day is variously reported for Nov 19-26. As of Nov 5, the amended S-1 filed Nov 2 still showed no price range.
items.notes: The timelines are second-hand (Bloomberg via XTB; Fortune and Fox Business via DecodetheFuture), and Anthropic has not confirmed them. A price-range amendment on EDGAR would be the next firm signal. Note: Anthropic makes the model writing this research.

items.text: The Senate passed both abortion bills without amendments, so they go straight to President Nawrocki. The bill restoring abortion for severe or lethal foetal defects passed 58–33 with 3 abstentions. The Criminal Code change ending penalties for helping with an abortion passed 56–34. Earlier, the Senate rejected PiS's motion to throw out the first bill.
items.outlet: Rynek Zdrowia; PAP via Portal Samorządowy; Interia
items.notes: Vote counts match across Rynek Zdrowia, PAP and Interia. No outlet reports any statement from the President's office yet. A veto is widely expected (see rule R-261026-06), but he has not said so.

items.text: The Sejm passed the resubmitted PIT/CIT bill on the evening of Nov 5, 236–207. On Nov 6 the Senate approved it without amendments, 63–31 with 1 abstention, and rejected PiS amendments for annual threshold indexation and a 180k zł threshold. The law adds a 24% PIT band for income of 130–150k zł and keeps 32% above that. It also sets 22% CIT for firms with revenue above €50m, raises the solidarity levy to 5%, and cuts the lump-sum (ryczałt) revenue limit to €250k. It now goes to President Nawrocki, who has 21 days to decide, but it must be published by the end of November to apply from 2027.
items.notes: Neither outlet reports a signal from Nawrocki's camp on signing or vetoing. The President's spokesman has previously called Domański the worst finance minister in history (rp.pl, Oct 27), and Nawrocki has vetoed tax rises before (alcohol excise).

items.text: The Senate passed the government's 'rule of law' act without amendments, 63–32, sending it to the President. The act voids KRS resolutions from March 2018 to May 2026 that recommended people for judicial appointment, except those concerning junior judges. The posts filled under them would become vacant and be re-advertised, and the judges concerned would return to their previous posts or professions. The opposition hopes Nawrocki will veto it.
items.notes: The Sejm passed the act on Oct 22, 231–200 with 6 abstentions. Neither outlet gives a count of affected judges. Right-leaning outlets call the targeted judges validly appointed. Coverage from the right on today's vote was not retrieved.

items.text: The Supreme Court rejected complaints by Bogdan Święczkowski and Bartłomiej Sochański against their suspension from Constitutional Tribunal duties. According to Onet, as cited by Polsat News, a single judge, Zbigniew Korzeniowski, ruled that the Supreme Court is not the proper body and referred the matter to the Tribunal itself. Six days earlier, Judge Korwin-Piotrowska had suspended both men as Tribunal president and vice-president.
items.notes: Headlines differ: Polsat says the complaint was 'dismissed' (oddalone), while XYZ and Tysol say the court will not hear it or refused to consider it. All agree it was referred to the Tribunal. WP reports that Justice Minister Żurek reacted, but that article was not read.

items.text: PSL leader Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz launched the second stage of his 'constitutional reset' of the Tribunal, with consultations, a public hearing and a signature drive. The draft amendment would let the National Assembly declare the Tribunal permanently unable to function, by a 3/5 vote on a KRS motion, and elect a new 15-judge bench. He claims 47 MPs back it, including Polska 2050 and Hołownia. He needs 92 signatures to submit it and is courting Konfederacja after talks with Mentzen. Sejm Marshal Czarzasty is sceptical about changing the constitution this term.
items.notes: Konfederacja has not committed. Żurek says the reset can be discussed only if it does not stop the Tribunal from working. A constitutional amendment needs 2/3 of the Sejm and an absolute majority in the Senate. The rp.pl link may be paywalled.

items.text: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola addressed the Sejm. She praised Poland for warning Europe about Russia earlier and for leading on defence, and said Poland and Europe need each other. During the speech, PiS MPs held up posters alleging a coup and a 'Tusk = Dictator' banner over the Tribunal dispute, and Tusk replied with a mocking selfie. Metsola also met Tusk, President Nawrocki and Senate Marshal Kidawa-Błońska, and collected the Jan Karski Eagle Award on behalf of the European Parliament.
items.notes: Framing differs. Euronews and rp.pl lead with her 'you were right about Russia' message. Judging only by headlines, since the articles could not be fetched, wPolityce focuses on the PiS protest and suggests Metsola 'may be shocked' by what PiS showed her and tried not to look at the banners. Nawrocki's talks with her covered climate policy, migration, the EU budget and enlargement.

items.text: A Tusk–Nawrocki one-on-one meeting still has no date. Asked in the Sejm on Friday whether the Palace had given any signal, Tusk spread his hands and shook his head. He said the goal was an agreement on the Tribunal in which no one is humiliated.
items.notes: The Palace has repeatedly said the meeting would be soon. Tusk says its date and place will be kept secret, so it may only become known afterwards.

items.text: The Sejm's Internal Affairs committee recommended rejecting PiS's no-confidence motion against Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński, 21–12. The motion accuses him of politicising the ministry, notably by deploying police at the Constitutional Tribunal. The Sejm scheduled a debate and vote for Friday afternoon and evening, and the coalition majority makes rejection likely, though the result was not confirmed at the time of writing.
items.notes: This is his third no-confidence motion. Kierwiński denied claims that police at the Tribunal lacked helmet ID numbers. The plenary result needs checking on Nov 7.

items.text: The Senate amended the bill capping doctors' pay and working time, 61–32 with 2 abstentions, so it goes back to the Sejm. The amendments raise the minimum employment to a quarter of a full-time post and drop the NFZ work ban for doctors who certify falsehoods. Separately, it passed without amendments the bill extending the hospital network to June 2029, 64–32.
items.notes: Details come from an RMF24/PAP roundup of the day's Senate votes.

items.text: Two Senate committees backed amendments to the anti-alcohol bill. The bill bans retail alcohol sales nationwide from 22:00 to 06:00 and bans alcohol advertising. The amendments would delay the start to June 1, 2027, ban discounts, bundles and loyalty schemes and home delivery of online orders, and allow some advertising of non-alcoholic beer. The Health Ministry called the beer change very harmful. The full Senate was due to vote on Nov 6, and if it adopts the amendments the bill returns to the Sejm.
items.notes: The plenary result was not confirmed. A Nov 5 Bizblog piece says the Senate already backed the bill with amendments, but no vote count was found, and the Nov 6 Rynek Zdrowia piece describes only committee votes. Nawrocki has vetoed alcohol excise increases before.

items.text: The Senate amended the bill creating state subsidies toward professional artists' social-security (ZUS) contributions, 62–33 with 1 abstention, so it returns to the Sejm. The amendments are clarifying and drafting changes.
items.notes: PulsHR puts the cost at more than 374 million zł. That figure is from earlier coverage and was not re-checked.

items.text: The Senate sent the President an Environmental Protection Law deregulation bill, 64–0 with 31 abstentions, and a special act helping homeowners cheated in the 'Czyste Powietrze' clean-air subsidy programme. The latter lets debts be suspended or written off and lets environmental funds pursue fraudulent firms directly. A housing and thermomodernisation financing bill, which shifts 141.5m zł from the 'Stop Smog' programme, was amended and returns to the Sejm.
items.notes: No vote count was reported for the Czyste Powietrze act.

items.text: Exercise KOALICJA 26.2, the first large drill of the coalition of the willing's planned Multinational Force Ukraine, will run Nov 9–22, mainly in Podkarpacie, with parts in France and Turkey. About 2,800 troops from 11 countries take part, nearly 2,000 of them Polish and about 300 British. A demonstration day at the Nowa Dęba range is on Nov 20. Poland would provide logistics through a support command in Bydgoszcz, and the force would be activated only after a ceasefire.
items.notes: The UK and France lead the exercise. The participants are Belgium, Estonia, France, Spain, the Netherlands, Lithuania, Germany, Poland, Sweden, Turkey and the UK. On Nov 3 Tusk warned that services expect possible sabotage or incursion attempts in the first half of November.

items.text: Warsaw hosted a Council of the Baltic Sea States foreign ministers' meeting. Ukrainian FM Andrii Sybiha visited, and FM Sikorski held bilateral talks with him and with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and the Estonian and Norwegian ministers. PAP said the agenda covered Europe's role in peace talks, coordination before a US–Ukraine–Russia meeting in Abu Dhabi, tighter sanctions on Russia, and air defence and energy aid for Ukraine.
items.notes: Based on a preview. What was said at the 16:30 joint press statements was not retrieved.

items.text: Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz handed out new command posts. Gen. Roman Łytkowski becomes deputy commander and Gen. Piotr Wańko chief of staff of the 2nd Polish Corps. Gen. Jerzy Kwika becomes head of air defence and is tasked with building up sensor reconnaissance. The minister cited Russian hybrid pressure, sabotage and airspace violations.
items.notes: He also said a 'Military Family Card' (Karta Rodziny Mundurowej) is nearly ready.

items.text: Organisers of the Nov 11 Independence March in Warsaw expect up to 500,000 people, against about 300,000 last year. They say the government's 'assault' on the Constitutional Tribunal will be a main theme, alongside sovereignty, migration and the EU. Kaczyński, Morawiecki, Bosak, Mentzen and Braun are reportedly expected, but the President's attendance is unconfirmed.
items.notes: The attendance figures are the organisers' own claims. 20 gatherings are registered in Warsaw for Nov 11.

items.text: Under the CPN programme, the Energy Ministry's maximum fuel prices for Nov 6 were 6.20 zł/l for 95 petrol, 6.93 zł for 98 and 7.91 zł for diesel. Forsal notes the government has not decided whether to extend the caps beyond Dec 31, and without an extension the limits, the cut VAT and the reduced excise end on Jan 1, 2027.
items.notes: Forsal's headline says the end of the caps is 'certain', but the article body says no decision has been made. The NBP projection assumes the caps end on Dec 31.

items.text: The Senate was due to elect Jacek Trela of NOWA Polska-Centrum as a new deputy Senate Marshal under a coalition agreement, and Kurier Lubelski reports he was elected.
items.notes: The Kurier Lubelski article was not read in full, so the vote count is unknown.

items.text: The city opened consultations (6-27 November) on a draft resolution that would freeze Clean Transport Zone (SCT) entry fees for 2027-2028 at today's rates: 100 zł a month, 2.50 zł an hour or 5 zł a day. Without it, the monthly fee would rise to 250 zł in January 2027 and 500 zł a year later. The draft is expected at the City Council in December; zone boundaries, emission rules and the end-2028 deadline do not change.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: The city announced the plan on 30 Oct; consultation details are on obywatelski.krakow.pl. Gibała's wider SCT changes (he has floated a referendum) will be presented separately.

items.text: The Supreme Audit Office (NIK) found that the fixed pay of management boards at four city companies (CGB Balicka, Wodociągi, MPEC and Arena Kraków) was set above the statutory cap in 2022-23, with about 980,000 zł overpaid, over 606,000 zł of it at Arena. NIK also questioned the appointment of a former developer to the water company's supervisory board, and said the city put 526m zł of capital into its companies without the required council resolution. The audit covers 2022-24; the city says it has started changing the pay resolutions.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: The NIK post-audit statement was sent to then-mayor Miszalski on 31 Oct 2025 and has only now been reported. The audit was not found on nik.gov.pl directly.

items.text: Deputy Mayor Jan Hoffman said the Music Centre (Centrum Muzyki) will stay under the city company ARMK for 2027, as a one-year compromise. The orchestras will rent it, with extra city subsidies covering the cost (ARMK puts it at up to 15m zł a year). The full transfer is planned for early 2028. Culture committee chair Magdalena Mazurkiewicz announced a resolution asking for the building to go to the cultural institutions.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Kracik's October drafts to hand the building to Sinfonietta Cracovia (about 7.8m zł in projected savings) were withdrawn by Gibała. The KRKnews article was seen only as a headline.

items.text: Gibała signed an order ending Szczęsny Filipiak's role as unpaid social adviser to the mayor on districts. Filipiak is a former head of Civic Platform (PO) in Kraków. Filipiak said he expected it and gave no comment on the reasons.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Gibała announced it on Facebook. It follows the 4 Nov abolition of Aleksandra Twaróg's post (E-261105-24).

items.text: The regional environment directorate (RDOŚ) said earthworks at a Ruczaj wetland near ul. Obozowa broke beaver-protection rules in the Nature Conservation Act. It ordered the work in the habitat to stop and referred the case to police. Developer ATAL, which is building a city retention reservoir as substitute investor, said it had not received the letter and was not working in the beaver area.
items.notes: RDOŚ had found no violation on 25 Oct and reversed after re-inspecting with a drone on 4 Nov. In September ATAL asked to cull six beavers, then withdrew the request.

items.text: The Małopolska Voivodeship Office began giving evacuation backpacks to public secondary schools, starting in Kraków. More than 540 schools across the region should have them by the end of 2026, paid for from the national civil protection programme. Fire service officers will also train school heads in crisis response.
items.notes: Voivode Krzysztof Jan Klęczar handed over the first backpack. The cost was not given.

items.text: Work on stage 2 of the Plac Sikorskiego revamp (a citizens' budget project worth about 920,000 zł) has restarted after the regional monument conservator granted a permit for archaeological supervision. The new completion date is the end of November, a month late.

The 204th Kraków derby, Wisła vs Cracovia in the Ekstraklasa, is tonight at 20:30 at Wisła's stadium on ul. Reymonta. LoveKraków reported that about 700 Cracovia fans set off flares and fireworks at their team's training on 4 November.
items.notes: No police or transit measures were found. Check ZTP/MPK for match-day changes.

items.text: A broken tram switch on ul. Dietla stopped trams on the morning of 6 November. Lines 12, 13, 18, 22, 71 and 78 were diverted, and replacement buses ran between Łagiewniki and Starowiślna. MPK expected trams to return around 10:00.
items.notes: It was not confirmed that service resumed.

items.text: The Union Cabinet approved an optional two-year 'Second Tour of Duty' for Agniveers, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh announced. The CDS said it covers the 75% of each batch who would otherwise leave after four years. The 25% merit-based absorption into regular service stays, and those who serve six years can later apply for regular enrolment under objective criteria. SP MP Awadhesh Prasad said an SP government would scrap the scheme within 24 hours.
items.outlet: ANI; NewsTak (Hindi); Patrika (Hindi); Rajnath Singh on X
items.notes: Corrects the previous brief, which said there was no official confirmation: the Cabinet approved it on Nov 4 and the Defence Minister announced it the same day (x.com/rajnathsingh/status/2117911265716875355). No PIB release or notification could be checked because PIB was not reachable. Pay, Seva Nidhi treatment and the start date were not reported. Patrika stresses that the extra two years do not guarantee a permanent job. Organiser frames it as a 'major overhaul'.

items.text: Hearing the Delhi-NCR air-pollution case, a Supreme Court bench led by CJI Surya Kant named vehicle emissions as a major cause. It said more court orders alone would not fix the problem, warned against putting the burden on poorer residents, and said it would rely on experts on a plea to close schools when AQI crosses a threshold. Delhi's AQI was about 389–391 ('very poor') on Friday morning, with 30 of 59 stations in the 'severe' band. The next hearing is Nov 16.
items.notes: No new directions were reported, and the court said it would pass further orders. AQI is from CPCB via Open (389 at 8 am) and PTI (391, 30 of 59 stations severe at 9 am). Aaj Tak's live feed said AQI was above 400 in most areas early in the morning. The green-cracker window (Nov 7–8) is unchanged.

items.text: Congress's Jairam Ramesh called for an urgent revamp of the National Clean Air Programme and an update to the 2009 air-quality standards. He cited a CREA analysis in which the three most polluted cities in October by PM2.5 were all in Uttar Pradesh: Baraut, Khora and Gajraula.
items.notes: An opposition statement that relies on CREA, an independent think tank. No government response was reported.

items.text: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan (Lalan) Singh said voter ID (EPIC), not only Aadhaar, will be used to identify beneficiaries of panchayat schemes. Rahul Gandhi called it a conspiracy and alleged that people removed from the rolls under SIR could also lose rations, pensions and MGNREGA work ('theft of rights'). Singh said Aadhaar alone would not be used and that biometric checks and EPIC numbers had been added. He accused Gandhi of twisting facts.
items.outlet: Amar Ujala (Hindi); IANS via Punjab Kesari English; Aaj Tak (Hindi)
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Amar Ujala and Aaj Tak (Hindi) carried only Gandhi's charge, with no government reply. IANS added Singh's clarification and rebuttal. Singh made the remark at a national workshop on the Jan Yojana Abhiyaan. No notification or order formalising the EPIC requirement was found. There was no ECI comment. Scroll and The Hindu could not be reached, so a left-liberal read of this story is missing.

items.text: Rahul Gandhi called state Congress chiefs and legislature-party leaders to a meeting in Delhi. Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar travelled to attend and to meet Union ministers, including over the sugarcane price row behind farmer protests in Karnataka.
items.notes: The meeting's agenda was not reported; SIR is the likely subject but that is not confirmed. UNI is paywalled. Note that Shivakumar is now CM and Siddaramaiah is a former CM (The Week, Nov 5).

items.text: At the INDIA bloc's 'Save Vote, Save Country' rally in Bengaluru, leaders passed five resolutions. They demand that SIR be withdrawn, that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign, that the CEC appointment law be repealed, and that Karnataka use its 2025 rolls rather than the final SIR rolls for coming taluk and zilla panchayat polls. The final rolls list 4.55 crore electors, about 99.3 lakh fewer than before the revision. The ECI says the exercise followed prescribed procedures.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Adds the resolutions and official roll figures to the previous item. The Week asks whether the movement is losing momentum beyond party cadres. The BJP and JD(S) criticised Shivakumar's sit-in outside the CEO's office.

items.text: A Supreme Court bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi issued contempt notice to all office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee over an Oct 12 post on its X account that told CJI Surya Kant to resign. The bench appointed an amicus to advise whether it is civil or criminal contempt and sought the Attorney General's help. The KPCC says a staffer posted it without approval, the post was deleted and an unconditional apology was given.
items.notes: The Week reports the KPCC's explanation in detail. Swarajya foregrounds the court's message and the bar bodies' condemnation, and gives the KPCC only an apology line. Office-bearers are exempt from appearing in person. No next date was reported. ThePrint/PTI calls the unit 'Keralam'.

items.text: In a 30-year-old interstate suit (Original Suit 2 of 1996), the Supreme Court ordered Punjab and Haryana to supply Himachal Pradesh 13,066 million units of arrears from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas projects over 20 lean seasons, instead of paying cash. Himachal's capital-cost liability of Rs 420.77 crore is offset against part of that energy. Punjab's objections were rejected.
items.outlet: Supreme Court judgment [2026 INSC 1200] via AdvocateKhoj
items.notes: Taken from the judgment text (bench: CJI Surya Kant, Joymalya Bagchi, V. Mohana). No news coverage or reactions from the states were found yet. The court stretched the repayment period from the 15 years the AG proposed to 20.

items.text: The Sensex jumped 1,718 points (2.17%) to 81,028 and the Nifty rose 2% to 25,030 on Dhanteras, extending the rally to a seventh session. The combined value of BSE-listed firms topped Rs 500 lakh crore for the first time. Brent was around $97–98 after fresh tanker attacks, while midcaps and smallcaps fell.
items.outlet: The Tribune; Kotak Neo; Business Standard
items.notes: Sources differ on the cause. Tribune analysts cite FII buying, lower crude and a stronger rupee. Kotak Neo says tanker attacks pushed crude higher. Business Standard's morning blog said rising oil and the global tech sell-off had kept the market flat at the open. No rupee level was given. ETV Bharat (opening report) quoted Geojit's view that India is the least exposed to the AI sell-off.

items.text: India hosted ASEAN ambassadors at the Navy's Information Fusion Centre for the Indian Ocean Region (Gurugram) for a briefing on maritime domain awareness, under the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.
items.notes: Comes just after the Navy's Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue and India's statements on seafarer safety amid the Gulf attacks.

items.text: Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said at a press conference that, if all goes well, he will be in the US early next week to meet Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Pentagon. He said they will discuss bases, the US troop presence and the alliance, but he would not give exact dates because the September meeting was cancelled at the last minute.
items.notes: This updates watch item W-261026-30. The meeting is not yet confirmed by the Pentagon.

items.text: Deputy Defence Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka said talks on a permanent US base are on track, that the final decision rests with President Trump, and that it should be settled within a few weeks. A Pentagon delegation led by Under Secretary Elbridge Colby discussed the base with Deputy Minister Paweł Zalewski at a Bergen Group meeting in Kraków on Nov 3, and National Security Bureau head Bartosz Grodecki met Colby a day earlier.
items.notes: This contradicts Błaszczak's (PiS) Nov 4 claim that the midterms have killed the base. The US side has made no public statement on the base after the Kraków talks. The Bergen Group is the US, Poland, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and Finland, and Denmark is joining.

items.text: President Nawrocki's aides Marcin Przydacz and Zbigniew Bogucki said the midterm result narrows the window for a permanent US base. They urged the government to move faster, noting there is still no implementing law. Kosiniak-Kamysz said the National Security Council had confirmed the base as a shared priority. PiS MP Radosław Fogiel said Nawrocki is speeding up the base talks, and Foreign Minister Sikorski mocked Polish right-wingers on X for distancing themselves from Trump.
items.notes: These are partisan statements from the presidential camp, the government and the opposition, not decisions. The government and the presidential palace both say they back the base but trade blame over the pace.

items.text: Foreign Minister Sikorski warned against Western Europe dealing with Russia over the heads of eastern Europeans, and PM Tusk urged allies to be wary of Putin's intentions. Euronews reports this comes as US-organised technical talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US resume in Abu Dhabi next week. Warsaw strongly opposes a reported US idea to restart Russian gas flows to Europe.
items.notes: Euronews is the only source for the details of the US gas plan. Sikorski also backed Meloni's call for a single European envoy chosen under the Lisbon Treaty framework (Costa or Kallas).

items.text: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie said he will decide early next week whether to pursue impeachment of Defense Secretary Hegseth, Kosiniak-Kamysz's counterpart for next week's planned Pentagon talks. Trump told ABC he is keeping Hegseth. The White House and State Dept also denied reports that Rubio is leaving.
items.outlet: RMF FM / RMF24 (citing NYT, ABC, Washington Post)
items.notes: This is mainly a US domestic story, logged here because it bears on the planned Polish–US defence meeting. The US desk may log it under US.

items.text: An analysis says the new Democratic Congress offers little near-term relief for Indian H-1B applicants, because the wage-weighted lottery and higher wage thresholds come from executive action. It says courts are the likelier route for any reversal. It also notes that a $100,000 fee was blocked by a federal court in June and that a new surcharge of about $103,000 has been proposed for cap-subject petitions.
items.notes: This is analysis citing unnamed analysts. The fee figures were not verified against USCIS or DHS.

items.text: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor rejected a report that he was being discussed as a possible successor to Secretary of State Rubio or chief of staff Susie Wiles. He called it false and said he has no interest in any other role.
items.notes: The original report cited 10 unnamed people familiar with internal talks and did not describe an offer.
